## Scope Adds opt-in AITER FlyDSL paged MXFP4 indexing for DeepSeek V4 on ROCm gfx950. Select with: ```bash --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' ``` FP8 remains the default. If the installed AITER does not expose the required stride-capable FP4 scorer APIs, vLLM warns and falls back to FP8. Supported ROCm configuration: - gfx950 - C4 compression - 64 query heads, head dimension 128 - 64-token compressed cache pages - DCP=PCP=1 This PR changes only the sparse indexer's Q/K cache precision and scorer path. It does not change model/MoE weights or the main attention KV cache. ## Implementation - The fused ROCm K producer writes packed E2M1 values and UE8M0 scales directly in the AITER preshuffled page layout. - The fused Q producer emits packed Q plus AITER's scale swizzle. - The cache adapter creates zero-copy value/scale views over vLLM's shared allocation. - Prefill and decode dispatch directly to AITER's paged FP4 scorers. - Folded index weights are rounded to BF16 for the AITER scorer contract. - Speculative rows are flattened before C4 length conversion. - Unsupported architectures, shapes and context-parallel configurations fail explicitly. The shared-pool page-stride and 64-bit address support is provided by ROCm/aiter#5518. ## Platform isolation The AITER path is selected only under `current_platform.is_rocm()`. - NVIDIA retains the existing DeepGEMM/CuTeDSL implementation. - CUDA FP4 packing and scale layout are unchanged. - FP8 remains the default on every platform. - ROCm-only packing uses a separate `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2_rocm` path. ## Tests Added focused host contract tests: - `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py` - default/auto/explicit FP8 remains unchanged - gfx950 and DCP/PCP gates - missing-AITER fallback - NVIDIA SM100-family gate without probing AITER - `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py` - existing FP8 dispatch and output dtype - ROCm FP4 packed-Q/scale shapes - unsupported ROCm shape rejection - existing NVIDIA Triton/CuTeDSL routing and scale views ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py \ tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py ``` Result: **35 passed**. These are host dispatch/layout tests; they are not NVIDIA GPU numerical validation. AITER scorer validation is in ROCm/aiter#5518 and covers: - exact FP4-dequant reference agreement (`cos=1.000000`) - direct FP4-vs-FP8 and both paths vs BF16 - random nonuniform Q/K and scales - shuffled physical pages and padded block-table strides - nonzero storage offsets - 2 GiB, 4 GiB and 4.608 GB physical offsets - ragged, tail, nonzero and empty windows - prefill and decode graph replay - deliberate page-map and scale-permutation sensitivity checks ## Decode schedule reuse The final commit preallocates a graph-stable FP4 CTA schedule buffer in the indexer metadata builder. The builder refreshes the schedule once per decode step; all sparse-indexer layers consume the same `cta_info` and `total_ctas`. The 512-CTA floor is unchanged. This does not change cache format, scorer math, top-k, BF16 weight handling, or NVIDIA paths. Validation: - focused host dispatch/schedule tests: **36 passed**; - AITER strided decode eager + graph replay: **PASS**; - historical isolated AgentX ablation: FP4 40.397M -> FP4+schedule 40.793M tokens/$, **+0.98% relative to FP4** and +3.66% vs the 39.354M baseline. The historical schedule result is one full3600 run and is superseded by the 2026-09-23 AgentX A/B below, which was measured with every commit of this PR present in both arms. ## Results All numbers in this section were re-measured on **2026-09-23** with the current PR head. They supersede the earlier serving tables, which are kept at the bottom for history. Common setup for every arm below: - Single node, 8 x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d` - `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache - vLLM overlay at `db7aa888e3`, AITER overlay carrying [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) + [ROCm/aiter#5518](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5518) - **Both arms** mount the AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) FP8 split-k `fp8_mqa_logits` overlay, so the baseline is FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 and the reported delta is attributable to FP4 indexing alone, not to ROCm/aiter#5603. - The MXFP4 arm additionally mounts this PR's five vLLM indexer files and AITER's three FlyDSL `pa_mqa_logits_fp4*` kernels, and sets `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`. Everything else - image, weights, serve flags, client, seed - is byte-identical. ### AgentX agentic-coding replay, TP1/DP8, concurrency 128 The primary end-to-end result. DP attention, MTP speculative decoding (3 tokens, synthetic acceptance 2.49), prefix caching enabled, full + piecewise CUDA graphs, 3,600 s measured window per arm after a 1,422-request warmup. Workload is the 393-entry `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` shared-prefix coding trace. The gain is larger at the tail than at the median: p95 ITL improves 24.7% and p95 interactivity 32.8%, versus 13.8%/16.0% at p50. Long-context agentic requests are exactly where the indexer dominates. 2. GPU KV-cache usage drops from 64.12% to 50.47%. Prefix-cache hit rate is effectively identical (89.77% vs 90.29%, against a 95.38%/95.51% trace-theoretical ceiling), so the throughput delta is not a cache-luck artifact. ### Kernel-level attribution Torch profiler capture of 4 engine iterations per arm, rank 0, same serve shape for both (TP8/DP1, `max_model_len` 10,240, `max_num_seqs` 64, prefix caching off, no MTP), same seeded synthetic client (ISL 8,000 / OSL 2,000, concurrency 64). Captured steps are mixed chunked-prefill + decode (2 context requests of ~8,135 tokens plus 54-59 generation requests per step) and are composition-matched across arms. | Indexer kernel group | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603, us | MXFP4 (this PR), us | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | mqa_logits scorer | 10,873.4 | 8,661.4 | **-20.34%** | | top-k selection | 12,169.6 | 9,019.5 | **-25.89%** | | KV compress + quant insert | 1,951.5 | 1,979.1 | **+1.41%** | | indexer quant-cache gather | 681.3 | 0.0 | removed | | FP4 prefill planning (new) | 0.0 | 290.6 | new | | | | | | | **Indexer path total** | **25,675.8** | **19,950.5** | **-22.30%** | | Shared (non-indexer) kernels | 1,220,442.9 | 1,216,620.0 | -0.31% | | All GPU kernels | 1,246,118.7 | 1,236,570.4 | -0.77% | Per engine step the indexer path costs 6,418.9 us on FP8 and 4,987.6 us on MXFP4, i.e. -1,431.3 us saved per step (-22.3%). The indexer is 2.1% of rank-0 GPU kernel time on FP8 and 1.6% on MXFP4. The saving splits roughly evenly between the two things this PR changes: the paged FP4 scorer replaces the gluon FP8 scorer plus its preshuffle (-20.34%), and the vLLM per-row top-k replaces AITER's radix top-k plus the prefill localisation pass (-25.89%). The FP8 path's separate `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache` kernel disappears entirely, and the new FP4 prefill-planning kernels run once per step for 290.6 us total, which is noise against the 5.7 ms saved. Note the scope difference: at this short-context shape the indexer is only 2.1% of GPU kernel time, so a 22.3% indexer saving is just -0.77% of total kernel time. That is consistent with, not contradictory to, the +9.65% AgentX result, where mean ISL is ~57K instead of 8K and the freed KV pool also raises the admitted batch. The trace establishes the mechanism; the AgentX table establishes the magnitude. ### Fixed 8,192-token input / 1,024-token output, TP8 Two A/Bs are reported here because they answer different questions, and the difference is entirely in **what the FP8 arm contains**. Serve configuration is identical in both: TP8/DP1, `max_model_len` 10240, `max_num_seqs` 64, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `gpu_memory_utilization` 0.86, prefix caching disabled, no MTP. With one run per arm (`single_run_warning=true`), the +2.65% remains suggestive, not a stable reproduction. ## Validation gaps - All four serving matrices (TP8 8k1k, DP8 8k1k, DP8 128k1k) were run once per arm; repeat runs are needed for variance, especially the DP8 128k cells. - The DP8 128k result disagrees with an earlier archived-overlay 128k run that showed C16/C64 gains; only the nightly-stack numbers above are reported as current-PR evidence. - NVIDIA GPU numerical tests were not run on this ROCm host. - Historical AgentX, fixed-length serving and AITER micro-benchmarks measure different scopes and are reported separately. ## AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) and FP4 prefill-planning follow-up Runtime: old `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, 8x MI355X TP8, ROCm 10 Sep-10 nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:72e90adf360ccffb231a098a15eadfb808719c029c6cd43f6386095064552b7e` (vLLM `2a02f6efe3`), AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) split-k plus ROCm/aiter#5518 stride/rebase APIs. Its apparent 18.30% wall-time improvement was a scheduler/cache artifact and is excluded. The corrected experiment sends one completion request containing all 16 token-ID prompts, disables prefix caching, and performs a shape-identical warmup. Median wall times were 2317.98 ms for FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603, 2320.69 ms for existing FP4, and 2326.11 ms for the new planner: all within 0.35%, i.e. no measurable end-to-end difference in this sample. The traces explain why kernel and wall-time results differ. The scheduler still split the logical request into 8-9 `execute_context` steps with different token buckets between arms. FP4 reduces indexer work, but the saved few milliseconds are diluted by roughly 2.3 seconds of model/MoE/attention execution. Therefore the kernel result is valid, while the earlier 18.30% wall-time attribution was not. ### Fixed 8K/1K service increment Two runs per FP4 arm; medians shown. FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 was measured once as the current baseline. All requests completed with zero failures. | C | Metric | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | Existing FP4 | New FP4 | New vs existing FP4 | New vs FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | Output tok/s | 689.14 | 674.83 | 681.62 | **+1.01%** | -1.21% | | 16 | Mean TTFT ms | 2040.03 | 2273.73 | 2226.27 | **-2.09%** | +9.00% | | 16 | Mean TPOT ms | 21.22 | 21.48 | 21.29 | **-0.89%** | +0.50% | | 64 | Output tok/s | 1527.11 | 1550.19 | 1552.95 | **+0.18%** | **+1.78%** | | 64 | Mean TTFT ms | 3960.79 | 4070.55 | 3988.94 | **-2.00%** | +0.71% | | 64 | Mean TPOT ms | 37.93 | 37.20 | 37.21 | +0.02% | **-1.91%** | The new planner therefore improves the mixed-context prefill path materially and adds a small, repeatable C16 fixed-load gain. C64 throughput is effectively flat versus existing FP4; the FP4 stack remains about 1.8% faster than FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 at C64. The fixed 8K prefill shapes selected `num_kv_splits=1`; therefore these service rows use the ROCm/aiter#5603 source but do not exercise split-K. AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) is not uniformly faster on this Triton build: exact source-only tests found one tested prefill shape improved while five were flat or slower. FP8 old/split logits, masks and top-k indices were bitwise identical; all 152 ROCm/aiter#5603 tests passed. ### Three-arm accuracy GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 64: | Arm | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 + AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | | Existing FP4 (`bd2f8acf`) | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | | New FP4 prefill planner | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | The prefill-planning change is accuracy-neutral on the full evaluation.

## Scope Adds opt-in AITER FlyDSL paged MXFP4 indexing for DeepSeek V4 on ROCm gfx950. Select with: ```bash --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' ``` FP8 remains the default. If the installed AITER does not expose the required stride-capable FP4 scorer APIs, vLLM warns and falls back to FP8. Supported ROCm configuration: - gfx950 - C4 compression - 64 query heads, head dimension 128 - 64-token compressed cache pages - DCP=PCP=1 This PR changes only the sparse indexer's Q/K cache precision and scorer path. It does not change model/MoE weights or the main attention KV cache. ## Implementation - The fused ROCm K producer writes packed E2M1 values and UE8M0 scales directly in the AITER preshuffled page layout. - The fused Q producer emits packed Q plus AITER's scale swizzle. - The cache adapter creates zero-copy value/scale views over vLLM's shared allocation. - Prefill and decode dispatch directly to AITER's paged FP4 scorers. - Folded index weights are rounded to BF16 for the AITER scorer contract. - Speculative rows are flattened before C4 length conversion. - Unsupported architectures, shapes and context-parallel configurations fail explicitly. The shared-pool page-stride and 64-bit address support is provided by ROCm/aiter#5518. ## Platform isolation The AITER path is selected only under `current_platform.is_rocm()`. - NVIDIA retains the existing DeepGEMM/CuTeDSL implementation. - CUDA FP4 packing and scale layout are unchanged. - FP8 remains the default on every platform. - ROCm-only packing uses a separate `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2_rocm` path. ## Tests Added focused host contract tests: - `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py` - default/auto/explicit FP8 remains unchanged - gfx950 and DCP/PCP gates - missing-AITER fallback - NVIDIA SM100-family gate without probing AITER - `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py` - existing FP8 dispatch and output dtype - ROCm FP4 packed-Q/scale shapes - unsupported ROCm shape rejection - existing NVIDIA Triton/CuTeDSL routing and scale views ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py \ tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py ``` Result: **35 passed**. These are host dispatch/layout tests; they are not NVIDIA GPU numerical validation. AITER scorer validation is in ROCm/aiter#5518 and covers: - exact FP4-dequant reference agreement (`cos=1.000000`) - direct FP4-vs-FP8 and both paths vs BF16 - random nonuniform Q/K and scales - shuffled physical pages and padded block-table strides - nonzero storage offsets - 2 GiB, 4 GiB and 4.608 GB physical offsets - ragged, tail, nonzero and empty windows - prefill and decode graph replay - deliberate page-map and scale-permutation sensitivity checks ## Decode schedule reuse The final commit preallocates a graph-stable FP4 CTA schedule buffer in the indexer metadata builder. The builder refreshes the schedule once per decode step; all sparse-indexer layers consume the same `cta_info` and `total_ctas`. The 512-CTA floor is unchanged. This does not change cache format, scorer math, top-k, BF16 weight handling, or NVIDIA paths. Validation: - focused host dispatch/schedule tests: **36 passed**; - AITER strided decode eager + graph replay: **PASS**; - historical isolated AgentX ablation: FP4 40.397M -> FP4+schedule 40.793M tokens/$, **+0.98% relative to FP4** and +3.66% vs the 39.354M baseline. The historical schedule result is one full3600 run and is superseded by the 2026-09-23 AgentX A/B below, which was measured with every commit of this PR present in both arms. ## Results All numbers in this section were re-measured on **2026-09-23** with the current PR head. They supersede the earlier serving tables, which are kept at the bottom for history. Common setup for every arm below: - Single node, 8 x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d` - `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache - vLLM overlay at `db7aa888e3`, AITER overlay carrying [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) + [ROCm/aiter#5518](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5518) - **Both arms** mount the AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) FP8 split-k `fp8_mqa_logits` overlay, so the baseline is FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 and the reported delta is attributable to FP4 indexing alone, not to ROCm/aiter#5603. - The MXFP4 arm additionally mounts this PR's five vLLM indexer files and AITER's three FlyDSL `pa_mqa_logits_fp4*` kernels, and sets `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`. Everything else - image, weights, serve flags, client, seed - is byte-identical. ### AgentX agentic-coding replay, TP1/DP8, concurrency 128 The primary end-to-end result. DP attention, MTP speculative decoding (3 tokens, synthetic acceptance 2.49), prefix caching enabled, full + piecewise CUDA graphs, 3,600 s measured window per arm after a 1,422-request warmup. Workload is the 393-entry `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` shared-prefix coding trace. The gain is larger at the tail than at the median: p95 ITL improves 24.7% and p95 interactivity 32.8%, versus 13.8%/16.0% at p50. Long-context agentic requests are exactly where the indexer dominates. 2. GPU KV-cache usage drops from 64.12% to 50.47%. Prefix-cache hit rate is effectively identical (89.77% vs 90.29%, against a 95.38%/95.51% trace-theoretical ceiling), so the throughput delta is not a cache-luck artifact. ### Kernel-level attribution Torch profiler capture of 4 engine iterations per arm, rank 0, same serve shape for both (TP8/DP1, `max_model_len` 10,240, `max_num_seqs` 64, prefix caching off, no MTP), same seeded synthetic client (ISL 8,000 / OSL 2,000, concurrency 64). TTFT is flat. This matches the isolated scorer's local-batch crossover and supersedes the previous prefix-cache-enabled TP8 8K/1K table. ### Accuracy Same nightly stack and servers, GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 64, `max_tokens=2048`. | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 baseline | 0.9484 | 0.000 | 119,898 | | This PR (MXFP4) | 0.9484 | 0.000 | 119,575 | FP4 indexing is accuracy-neutral on GSM8K: identical accuracy, no invalid responses in either arm. The only fixed scheduling choice is the same decode floor used by ATOM: `parallel_unit_num=max(512, rows)` with `block_k=256`. Output TPS is additionally affected by different realized output lengths (943 vs 913 mean tokens). The corrected experiment sends one completion request containing all 16 token-ID prompts, disables prefix caching, and performs a shape-identical warmup. +#### Experimental gfx950 MXFP4 indexer
+
+On ROCm gfx950, DeepSeek V4 can select the direct-paged AITER FlyDSL
+indexer with `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`.
+The default indexer cache remains FP8. MXFP4 changes indexer Q/K precision
+and can change top-k selection; validate model accuracy for the workload.
+
+This path integrates with AITER FlyDSL FP4 kernels that support explicit
+shared-cache page strides, 64-bit physical-page addressing, and precomputed
+decode/prefill schedules. If the installed AITER build lacks the required
+kernel or schedule interfaces, vLLM falls back to the default fp8
+indexer rather than using an incompatible layout. It supports 64-token
+compressed pages, C4 compression,
+64 query heads of dimension 128, and DCP/PCP size 1. Speculative rows are
+flattened before C4 length division. The metadata builder computes prefill
+windows and AITER schedules once per step for reuse across indexer layers.
+Decode schedules use builder-owned storage refreshed before graph replay.
+Prefill chunks are bounded by query rows times the maximum compressed request
+length, rather than the sum of gathered request lengths.

 Performance: no measurable end-to-end difference
 - At kernel level, the tuned grid helps only at small decode batches (rows ≤ 8): 7–29% faster, but that is only about 0.3–1.5 us per call. At rows 16/64 the two are equal.
 - Serving A/B on 8× MI355X, TP1/DP8, mxfp4 indexer, 3 runs per arm. The only difference between arms is the CTA count:

 ┌──────┬────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
 │ ISL  │ C  │ 512 TPOT ms (3 runs)  │ tuned TPOT ms (3 runs) │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 8K   │ 1  │ 21.0 / 21.0 / 21.1         │ 21.1 / 21.1 / 21.0     │

 │ 128K │ 64 │ 166.8 / 170.9 / 184.4 │ 183.6 / 180.7 / 171.2  │
 └──────┴────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

 All C1–C64 cells overlap within run-to-run noise. The kernel saves about 10–45 us per step, while TPOT is 20–180 ms. Also, at 128K the compressed max_seq_len is 33280, and with about 8 rows per rank the selector already picks
 512.

 Switching to the default selector as-is would crash

 ```
ValueError: cta_info_out must have shape (at least 1280, 4), got (512, 4).
 ```
